about: The rules, deadlines and checklist boxes of this playbook in everyday words, for people who are not developers or lawyers, written with scripts/plain-language.py and each one checked against its original for meaning. "from" is a fingerprint of the original an entry was written from: when the original changes, apps show the original until this file is written again.

ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-FONTSCALING.title: Text size that ignores the phone's settings
ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-FONTSCALING.problem:
Your app sets text sizes in a fixed unit (dp).
So text won't grow when people pick bigger text on their phone.
ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-FONTSCALING.fix:
Always set text sizes in the unit that scales (sp).
Then the phone's text size setting works.

ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-HIGHCONTRAST.title: Fixed colors that ignore high contrast settings
ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-HIGHCONTRAST.problem:
Your app's screens use fixed color codes.
They don't come from your app's theme.
So high contrast settings can't change them.
ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-HIGHCONTRAST.fix:
Use named colors from your app's theme or color files.
Then your app follows high contrast settings by itself.

ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-SCANNER.title: Buttons too small to tap
ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-SCANNER.problem:
Some tappable items are smaller than 48 by 48 screen units (dp).
Their width, height or padding makes the touch area too small.
ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-SCANNER.fix:
Make every tappable item at least 48 by 48 screen units.
- Add padding around it.
- Or set a minimum width and height.

ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-TALKBACK.title: Screen reader can't describe your app
ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-TALKBACK.problem:
Images or controls have no text label for the screen reader (TalkBack).
Or they are wrongly hidden from it.
So people using it can't tell what they are.
ANDROID-ACCESSIBILITY-TALKBACK.fix:
Give each useful image and control a clear text label (contentDescription).
Check the screen reader shows and hides the right items.

ANDROID-ACCOUNT-DELETION-URL.title: Accounts with no way to delete them
ANDROID-ACCOUNT-DELETION-URL.problem:
Your app lets people make an account.
But they can't delete it inside the app.
And there's no web page for asking to delete their data.
ANDROID-ACCOUNT-DELETION-URL.fix:
Do both of these.
- Let people delete their account inside the app.
- Add a public data deletion web address in Play Console.

ANDROID-ADVERTISING-ID.title: Advertising ID used without an opt out
ANDROID-ADVERTISING-ID.problem:
Google checks if your app does either of these:
- Declares or uses the ad ID permission (AD_ID).
- Reads the advertising ID.
Then it checks your app and privacy policy.
They give no way to opt out or ask for deletion.
ANDROID-ADVERTISING-ID.fix:
Ask your developer to declare the ad ID permission.
- Put it in the app's settings file (AndroidManifest.xml).
- Handle opt out requests the way Google Play requires.
- Handle deletion requests the way Google Play requires.

ANDROID-DYNAMIC-CODE-LOADING.title: Downloading new code while the app runs
ANDROID-DYNAMIC-CODE-LOADING.problem:
Your app downloads code and runs it while it's open.
Google doesn't allow this.
If your app targets API level 37, writable native libraries won't load.
ANDROID-DYNAMIC-CODE-LOADING.fix:
Put all your app's code inside the app you upload.
Your server may only send data, never code that runs.

ANDROID-HEALTH-PERMISSIONS.title: Reading health data without Health Connect setup
ANDROID-HEALTH-PERMISSIONS.problem:
Your app reads health or fitness data, like steps or heart rate.
It uses Google's health data hub (Health Connect).
But it doesn't declare this properly, or has no health privacy policy.
ANDROID-HEALTH-PERMISSIONS.fix:
Do all three.
- List the Health Connect permissions your app uses.
- Fill in the Health Connect form in Play Console.
- Keep a separate privacy policy just for health data.

ANDROID-INSECURE-BACKUP.title: Backups that copy logins and private data
ANDROID-INSECURE-BACKUP.problem:
Your app allows phone backups (allowBackup is true).
But it doesn't leave login details or databases out of them.
So private data can end up in backups.
ANDROID-INSECURE-BACKUP.fix:
Pick one.
- Turn backups off (allowBackup="false").
- Or set backup rules that leave out logins and databases.

ANDROID-OVERLAY-TAPJACKING.title: Drawing over other apps, a malware sign
ANDROID-OVERLAY-TAPJACKING.problem:
Your app asks to draw on top of other apps (SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW).
That can trick people into tapping things they didn't mean to.
Google sees it plus an accessibility service as a strong malware sign.
ANDROID-OVERLAY-TAPJACKING.fix:
Remove any misuse of drawing over other apps.
Google takes action against apps that combine it with an accessibility service.

ANDROID-QUERY-ALL-PACKAGES.title: Asking to see all installed apps
ANDROID-QUERY-ALL-PACKAGES.problem:
Your app asks to see every app on the phone (QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES).
Google allows this only for certain approved uses.
ANDROID-QUERY-ALL-PACKAGES.fix:
Do one of these.
- Name only the apps you need to see (a queries list).
- Or show that your app fits one of Google's approved uses.

ANDROID-RUNTIME-PERMISSIONS.title: Asking for sensitive permissions without checks
ANDROID-RUNTIME-PERMISSIONS.problem:
Your app asks for sensitive permissions, like camera, contacts or storage.
It has one of these gaps:
- It doesn't check permissions while it runs.
- It doesn't clearly explain to people why it needs them.
ANDROID-RUNTIME-PERMISSIONS.fix:
Ask your developer to change how permissions work.
- Check each permission while the app runs.
- Show a clear reason if someone says no.
- Keep the app working smoothly when people say no.

GOOGLE-PHOTO-VIDEO-PERMISSIONS-DECLARATI.title: Full photo access without the photo picker
GOOGLE-PHOTO-VIDEO-PERMISSIONS-DECLARATI.problem:
Your app asks to read all photos and videos.
Yet it never uses the phone's built-in photo picker.
Apps built for newer Android (API 33 or higher) face two rules.
- Full access only when the picker can't do a core job.
- Every app keeping full access must fill in a Play Console form.
GOOGLE-PHOTO-VIDEO-PERMISSIONS-DECLARATI.fix:
Use the built-in photo picker for one-time picks.
Keep full access only for a core gallery-style feature.
Then fill in the Photo and Video Permissions form in Play Console.

ANDROID-USER-DATA-DISCLOSURE.title: No clear notice before reading private data
ANDROID-USER-DATA-DISCLOSURE.problem:
Your app reads private data without a notice or asking first.
Google checks this for access to:
- contacts
- text messages (SMS)
- call history
- accounts on the phone
- all files
ANDROID-USER-DATA-DISCLOSURE.fix:
Show a clear notice in the app before you collect this data.
Then get a clear yes from each person.

APPLE-2.1-CLOUD-NOT-IN-PRODUCTION.title: iCloud setup not live for real users
APPLE-2.1-CLOUD-NOT-IN-PRODUCTION.problem:
Your app uses iCloud, but its setup is only in test mode.
So the feature breaks for the reviewer on the real build.
APPLE-2.1-CLOUD-NOT-IN-PRODUCTION.fix:
Before you submit, move these from test to live mode.
- Your iCloud data layout (CloudKit schema).
- Your iCloud storage containers.

APPLE-2.1-DEBUG-FEATURES.title: Test tools left in the release version
APPLE-2.1-DEBUG-FEATURES.problem:
Your release version still shows test tools.
- Debug menus
- Test logins
- Hidden developer back doors
They aren't locked to test versions only.
APPLE-2.1-DEBUG-FEATURES.fix:
Lock test tools behind a test only setting (debug compile flag).
Then they never reach the public version.

APPLE-2.1-MISSING-DEMO-ACCOUNT.title: No demo account for a login app
APPLE-2.1-MISSING-DEMO-ACCOUNT.problem:
Your app has a login, but you gave the reviewer no demo account.
The reviewer can't get in to test it.
APPLE-2.1-MISSING-DEMO-ACCOUNT.fix:
Before you submit, fill in the Notes for Review box.
- Add a working demo account.
- Add steps to test the app live.

APPLE-2.1-PLACEHOLDER-CONTENT.title: Placeholder text left in the app
APPLE-2.1-PLACEHOLDER-CONTENT.problem:
Your app still has filler or test content, like:
- lorem ipsum
- TODO or FIXME
- placeholder or dummy text
- test data
- example.com
APPLE-2.1-PLACEHOLDER-CONTENT.fix:
Replace all filler text, images and files with real content.
Do this before you submit.

APPLE-2.1-REVIEW-NOTES-INCOMPLETE.title: Review notes missing a required section
APPLE-2.1-REVIEW-NOTES-INCOMPLETE.problem:
For a new app, review notes need six sections. Yours skips one.
- A screen recording on a real device.
- What the app is for.
- How to get in, with test logins.
- Outside services the app uses.
- Differences between countries or regions.
- Documents for regulated industries.
APPLE-2.1-REVIEW-NOTES-INCOMPLETE.fix:
Fill in all six sections.
Use the review notes template (templates/REVIEW-NOTES-TEMPLATE.md).

APPLE-2.1-STAGING-BACKEND.title: App connects to a test server
APPLE-2.1-STAGING-BACKEND.problem:
Your release build points to a test server, not your live one.
The server address (API base URL) has one of these:
- localhost or 127.0.0.1
- staging or dev
- ngrok
APPLE-2.1-STAGING-BACKEND.fix:
Point the release build at your live server.
Check it stays up while Apple reviews your app.

APPLE-2.3-AGE-RATING-2026.title: New age rating questions not answered
APPLE-2.3-AGE-RATING-2026.problem:
Apple added new age rating questions for 13 plus, 16 plus and 18 plus.
From 31 January 2026, you can't submit updates until you answer them.
APPLE-2.3-AGE-RATING-2026.fix:
Answer the new age rating questions in App Store Connect.
Do this for every app you have.

APPLE-2.3-CROSS-PLATFORM-REFERENCE.title: Mentions other platforms or app stores
APPLE-2.3-CROSS-PLATFORM-REFERENCE.problem:
Your app or store page text names other platforms or app stores.
Examples are Android, Google Play or other app marketplaces.
APPLE-2.3-CROSS-PLATFORM-REFERENCE.fix:
Remove every mention of other platforms and app stores.
Check both the app and your store page text.

APPLE-2.3-FUTURE-FUNCTIONALITY.title: Store page promises features not built yet
APPLE-2.3-FUTURE-FUNCTIONALITY.problem:
Your store page or app text promises things this version doesn't do.
This includes words like coming soon or beta.
APPLE-2.3-FUTURE-FUNCTIONALITY.fix:
Describe only what this version does today.
Remove coming soon and any promised future features from your store page.

APPLE-2.3-NEGATIVE-APPLE-SENTIMENT.title: Store page speaks badly of Apple
APPLE-2.3-NEGATIVE-APPLE-SENTIMENT.problem:
Your store page text mentions an iOS bug.
Or it says something negative or unkind about Apple.
APPLE-2.3-NEGATIVE-APPLE-SENTIMENT.fix:
Remove any mention of iOS bugs from your store page text.
Remove anything negative about Apple too.

APPLE-2.3.4-DEVICE-FRAMES-PREVIEW.title: Preview video shows a device frame
APPLE-2.3.4-DEVICE-FRAMES-PREVIEW.problem:
Your app preview video puts the app inside a picture of a device.
Apple wants the app shown full screen.
APPLE-2.3.4-DEVICE-FRAMES-PREVIEW.fix:
Record the preview video full screen on the device.
Don't add a device frame on top.

APPLE-2.4.5-UNUSED-ENTITLEMENTS.title: Permissions from Apple you don't use
APPLE-2.4.5-UNUSED-ENTITLEMENTS.problem:
Your app lists a permission from Apple (entitlement) it doesn't use.
Apple asks you to explain it, which blocks review.
Temporary exception permissions get checked even more closely.
APPLE-2.4.5-UNUSED-ENTITLEMENTS.fix:
Remove every permission from Apple your app doesn't actively use.
Check each one against what your code really does.

APPLE-2.5.1-PRIVATE-API.title: Uses hidden or outdated Apple code
APPLE-2.5.1-PRIVATE-API.problem:
Your app uses Apple features that aren't public (private APIs).
Or it uses outdated Apple toolkits that are being phased out.
APPLE-2.5.1-PRIVATE-API.fix:
Use only public, documented Apple features.
Use current Apple toolkits, not outdated ones.

APPLE-3.1.1-EXTERNAL-PAYMENT.title: Selling digital goods outside Apple's payment system
APPLE-3.1.1-EXTERNAL-PAYMENT.problem:
Your app sells digital content without Apple's payment system.
The reviewer finds one of these used for that content:
- A web checkout
- Outside payment add-on code
APPLE-3.1.1-EXTERNAL-PAYMENT.fix:
Sell all digital goods through Apple's in app payments (StoreKit).
The only exception is a type of app Apple's rules list as exempt.

APPLE-3.1.2-MISLEADING-PRICING.title: Monthly price shown bigger than real charge
APPLE-3.1.2-MISLEADING-PRICING.problem:
Your payment screen shows a yearly plan's monthly price in large type.
The real amount charged appears small.
This misleads people about the price.
APPLE-3.1.2-MISLEADING-PRICING.fix: Show the real amount charged at least as clearly as any monthly figure.

APPLE-4.0-SIWA-UX.title: Poor use of Sign in with Apple
APPLE-4.0-SIWA-UX.problem:
Your app handles Sign in with Apple the wrong way.
- It asks again for name or email Apple already gave.
- Its Apple button isn't the standard one.
- It puts the Apple button below other social logins.
- It refuses the private email address Apple can give.
APPLE-4.0-SIWA-UX.fix:
Follow Apple's rules for its login.
- Use the name and email Apple sends. Don't ask again.
- Use Apple's standard button.
- Make it at least as easy to see as other logins.
- Accept Apple's private email addresses.

APPLE-4.2-WEB-WRAPPER.title: App is just your website, nothing more
APPLE-4.2-WEB-WRAPPER.problem:
Your app mostly loads your website in one screen.
It has little code of its own.
Apple turns down apps that add nothing to the website.
APPLE-4.2-WEB-WRAPPER.fix:
Give people something the website can't.
- Features built into the app itself.
- Things that work offline.
- Links with the phone's own hardware and tools.
- Content the website doesn't have.

APPLE-4.8-SOCIAL-LOGIN-ONLY.title: Social login with no private option
APPLE-4.8-SOCIAL-LOGIN-ONLY.problem:
Your app offers login with Facebook, Google or similar.
It doesn't offer Sign in with Apple.
It has no equal login that protects privacy either.
APPLE-4.8-SOCIAL-LOGIN-ONLY.fix:
Add Sign in with Apple or an equal login.
- It must only collect name and email.
- It must let people keep their email private.

APPLE-5.1.1-MISSING-PRIVACY-POLICY.title: No privacy policy
APPLE-5.1.1-MISSING-PRIVACY-POLICY.problem:
Reviewers can't find your privacy policy.
Your app's store settings have no link to it.
Your app has no link to it either.
APPLE-5.1.1-MISSING-PRIVACY-POLICY.fix:
Publish a privacy policy online.
- Add its link in Apple's developer dashboard (App Store Connect).
- Add a link to it inside your app.

APPLE-5.1.1-MISSING-USAGE-DESCRIPTION.title: Phone feature used without saying why
APPLE-5.1.1-MISSING-USAGE-DESCRIPTION.problem:
Your app's code uses a sensitive phone feature.
Your app's settings file (Info.plist) gives no reason for it.
APPLE-5.1.1-MISSING-USAGE-DESCRIPTION.fix:
For each sensitive feature, add its matching reason line.
Make each reason specific to your app.

APPLE-5.1.1-NO-ACCOUNT-DELETION.title: No way to delete an account
APPLE-5.1.1-NO-ACCOUNT-DELETION.problem:
People can create an account in your app.
They can't delete it from inside the app.
APPLE-5.1.1-NO-ACCOUNT-DELETION.fix:
Let people delete their account inside the app.
This applies to any app that lets people sign up.

APPLE-5.1.1-UNNECESSARY-DATA.title: Asking for personal details you don't need
APPLE-5.1.1-UNNECESSARY-DATA.problem:
Your sign up or setup screens force people to share personal details.
For example, phone number, gender, marital status, birth date or home address.
Apple says no if your main feature doesn't need them.
What counts as needed depends on your app.
APPLE-5.1.1-UNNECESSARY-DATA.fix:
Make personal fields optional unless your main feature needs them.
Only require details tied directly to your main feature.

APPLE-5.1.1-VAGUE-PURPOSE-STRING.title: Vague or empty permission message
APPLE-5.1.1-VAGUE-PURPOSE-STRING.problem:
A permission message in your app is empty or vague.
Words like "needs access" or "required" don't say why.
APPLE-5.1.1-VAGUE-PURPOSE-STRING.fix:
Rewrite each permission message.
Name the real feature that uses that permission.

APPLE-5.1.2-AI-NO-CONSENT-MODAL.title: Sending personal data to AI without asking
APPLE-5.1.2-AI-NO-CONSENT-MODAL.problem:
Your app has add-on code from an outside AI company.
It may send personal data to that company.
People don't first see a pop-up naming the company.
APPLE-5.1.2-AI-NO-CONSENT-MODAL.fix:
Show a pop-up asking permission first.
- Name the AI company.
- Say what kinds of data you'll send.
- Show it before any personal data leaves the app.

APPLE-5.1.2-MISSING-ATT.title: Tracking without Apple's tracking pop-up
APPLE-5.1.2-MISSING-ATT.problem:
Your app has add-on code for tracking or ads.
- It never shows Apple's tracking permission pop-up.
- It has no message explaining the tracking.
APPLE-5.1.2-MISSING-ATT.fix:
Show Apple's tracking pop-up (App Tracking Transparency) before tracking people across apps.
Also add the message that explains your tracking.

APPLE-5.2.5-APPLE-DEVICE-IMAGE.title: Apple devices or logo in your images
APPLE-5.2.5-APPLE-DEVICE-IMAGE.problem:
A reviewer checks your app icon and screenshots by hand.
They show an Apple device or the Apple logo.
Or they suggest Apple backs your app.
APPLE-5.2.5-APPLE-DEVICE-IMAGE.fix: Remove Apple devices and Apple marks from your icon and screenshots.

APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-COLORCONTRAST.title: Fixed colors ignore phone display settings
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-COLORCONTRAST.problem:
Your app uses fixed custom colors.
They don't change for these settings:
- Dark mode and light mode
- High contrast
- Darker system colors (isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled)
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-COLORCONTRAST.fix:
Use system colors that change on their own.
Or watch the darker colors setting and adjust contrast while your app runs.

APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-DYNAMICTYPE.title: Text size ignores the phone setting
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-DYNAMICTYPE.problem:
Your app uses fixed text sizes.
They don't grow or shrink with the phone's text size setting.
Or text scaling is switched off (adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory).
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-DYNAMICTYPE.fix:
Ask your developer to use text styles that scale.
- Older screens: built-in text styles (preferredFont).
- Newer screens: system or relative text styles.
- Keep automatic text scaling switched on.

APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-HAPTICS.title: No buzz feedback when people tap things
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-HAPTICS.problem:
Your app gives no buzz feedback (CoreHaptics) when people use it.
This covers:
- Every part people can tap, swipe or use
- Buttons
- Custom controls
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-HAPTICS.fix:
Add a small buzz when people use these parts.
- Buttons
- Toggles
- Swipe actions
Your developer can use Apple's tap buzz tool (UIImpactFeedbackGenerator).
A selection buzz also works.

APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-KEYBOARD.title: Can't move around with a keyboard
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-KEYBOARD.problem:
People with a real keyboard can't move around your app.
This shows up in custom text editors and complex screens.
They lack keyboard shortcuts and focus support.
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-KEYBOARD.fix:
Let people move through your app with a real keyboard.
- Older screens: add keyboard shortcuts (keyCommands).
- Newer screens: let items take keyboard focus.

APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-REDUCEMOTION.title: Animations ignore the Reduce Motion setting
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-REDUCEMOTION.problem:
Your app plays custom animations and screen changes.
It never checks if the person turned on Reduce Motion.
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-REDUCEMOTION.fix:
Check the Reduce Motion setting (isReduceMotionEnabled).
When it's on, turn off or calm down extra animations.

APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-VOICEOVER.title: VoiceOver screen reader support is incomplete
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-VOICEOVER.problem:
Some buttons, controls or images have no spoken labels.
VoiceOver can't tell people what they are.
APPLE-ACCESSIBILITY-VOICEOVER.fix:
Give each control and image the right spoken details.
- A label saying what it is
- A hint saying what it does
- Traits, such as being a button

APPLE-ACCOUNT-DELETION-WEAK.title: Account deletion only by email or pause
APPLE-ACCOUNT-DELETION-WEAK.problem:
People can't fully delete their account inside your app.
The only way out is one of these:
- An email link
- A web form outside your app
- A pause that doesn't delete anything
APPLE-ACCOUNT-DELETION-WEAK.fix:
Let people delete their account and its data inside your app.
Pausing the account or a web form outside isn't enough.

APPLE-EXPORT-COMPLIANCE-MISSING.title: Missing encryption answer stalls your build
APPLE-EXPORT-COMPLIANCE-MISSING.problem:
Your app doesn't say if it uses encryption.
This answer belongs in the app's settings file (Info.plist).
Without it, every build gets stuck before review.
It never reaches a reviewer.
APPLE-EXPORT-COMPLIANCE-MISSING.fix:
Set the encryption answer in your app's settings file.
Its name is ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption.
Pick the exempt answer if your app only uses standard secure web links (HTTPS).

APPLE-GAMBLING-BRAZIL-LICENSE.title: No Brazil betting license given to Apple
APPLE-GAMBLING-BRAZIL-LICENSE.problem:
Your app has gambling or betting features on the Brazil store.
Your review notes for Apple have no valid license.
It must be a fixed-odds license from Brazil's Secretariat of Prizes and Bets (SPA).
APPLE-GAMBLING-BRAZIL-LICENSE.fix:
Do these steps:
- Answer Yes to gambling in the age rating questions.
- This sets your Brazil age rating to A18.
- Add the valid SPA license to your review notes (App Review Information).
- Send in a new app version so Apple can check it.
Only editing your review notes won't start the check.
Apple said this on 8 May 2026.

APPLE-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.title: Missing the privacy file Apple asks for
APPLE-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.problem:
Apple finds one of these in your app.
- It uses phone features Apple watches, with no privacy file.
- It has a widely used add-on, with no privacy file.
- An add-on has no signed privacy file of its own.
Since 2024, Apple blocks these uploads.
APPLE-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.fix:
Ask your developer to add Apple's privacy file (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy).
- Give an approved reason for each feature used.
- List any web addresses used for tracking.
- Check every add-on ships its own signed file.

APPLE-PRIVACY-NUTRITION-LABELS.title: Missing Apple privacy labels for collected data
APPLE-PRIVACY-NUTRITION-LABELS.problem:
Your app collects private data about people.
Examples are email, phone number, name or location.
But it doesn't list this data where Apple expects it.
APPLE-PRIVACY-NUTRITION-LABELS.fix:
Do two things.
- List each data type in Apple's privacy file (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy).
- Fill in the matching privacy labels in App Store Connect.

APPLE-RESTORE-PURCHASES-MISSING.title: No way to restore past purchases
APPLE-RESTORE-PURCHASES-MISSING.problem:
Your app sells things through Apple's payment system.
There's no way for people to get past purchases back.
APPLE-RESTORE-PURCHASES-MISSING.fix:
Add a Restore Purchases button people can see.
You need it if you sell either of these.
- Items bought once that people keep.
- Subscriptions that don't renew on their own.

BOTH-AI-GENERATED-CONTENT.title: AI content with no safety tools
BOTH-AI-GENERATED-CONTENT.problem:
Your app uses AI to create content or images.
It lacks filtering, reporting, blocking, an age rating or abuse safeguards.
Apple treats AI output like content users post.
Google has its own rule for AI content.
Since 16 October 2026, Apple names AI content creation apps.
They must stop and remove intimate images shared without consent, AI ones too.
BOTH-AI-GENERATED-CONTENT.fix:
Ask your developer to add these:
- Moderation, reporting and blocking.
- An accurate age rating.
- Abuse safeguards.
Stop the AI making adult, deepfake, face swap or undress images.

BOTH-E-EVIDENCE-COMPLIANCE-MISSING.title: No EU contact for official data requests
BOTH-E-EVIDENCE-COMPLIANCE-MISSING.problem:
Your app handles user data in the EU.
EU authorities can order you to hand over or keep user data.
You're missing at least one of these:
- a business base or legal representative in the EU
- a plan to answer orders within 10 days
- a plan to answer emergencies within 8 hours
BOTH-E-EVIDENCE-COMPLIANCE-MISSING.fix:
Set up an EU contact and a response plan.
- Have a business base or legal representative in the EU.
- Share their contact details by 18 August 2026.
- Plan to send user data safely within 8 hours in emergencies.

BOTH-FINGERPRINTING.title: Tracking people with a device fingerprint
BOTH-FINGERPRINTING.problem:
Your app tracks people with a lasting ID.
It builds this ID from phone hardware or settings.
Apple bans this even when people agree to tracking.
BOTH-FINGERPRINTING.fix:
Don't build device fingerprints.
If you truly need tracking, use the phone's own ad ID.
Only use it when people agree.

BOTH-GPSR-COMPLIANCE-MISSING.title: Missing EU product safety details
BOTH-GPSR-COMPLIANCE-MISSING.problem:
Your app's shop or product listings are missing EU safety details.
- The maker's email address.
- The maker's postal address.
- Product safety warnings.
BOTH-GPSR-COMPLIANCE-MISSING.fix:
This covers any consumer product supplied in the EU, sold or given away.
Show these clearly on the listing or in your app.
- The maker's email address.
- The maker's postal address.
- Any safety warnings that apply.

BOTH-LOOTBOX-ODDS.title: Random rewards with hidden odds
BOTH-LOOTBOX-ODDS.problem:
Your app sells random rewards, like loot boxes or gacha.
It doesn't show the odds before people buy.
BOTH-LOOTBOX-ODDS.fix: Show the odds of every random reward before people pay.

BOTH-METADATA-DECORATION.title: Store page text too long or decorated
BOTH-METADATA-DECORATION.problem:
Your app name or icon has one of these problems.
- The name is over 30 characters, the limit in both stores.
- The name has emoji.
- The name is in all capital letters.
- The name or icon claims a rank or price.
Examples are number one, best, top or free.
BOTH-METADATA-DECORATION.fix:
Keep each piece of store page text within its limit.
Then clean up the name and icon.
- Remove emoji.
- Don't use all capital letters.
- Remove claims like number one, best, top or free.

BOTH-SDK-SUPPLY-CHAIN.title: Add-on code breaks rules for you
BOTH-SDK-SUPPLY-CHAIN.problem:
Add-on code in your app does things your app doesn't declare.
- It asks for permissions.
- It tracks users.
- It acts in other ways you haven't declared.
You're responsible for what your add-ons do.
BOTH-SDK-SUPPLY-CHAIN.fix:
Check every add-on, including ones already in your app.
- Keep each one up to date.
- Remove any that collect or share data your app doesn't declare.

BOTH-SECURE-STORAGE.title: Login keys saved without protection
BOTH-SECURE-STORAGE.problem:
Your app saves login details or access keys in plain files.
These files are not locked.
The phone's secure storage should hold them instead.
BOTH-SECURE-STORAGE.fix:
Move all private data and access keys into the phone's secure storage.
- On iPhone, use Apple's secure storage (Keychain).
- On Android, use Android's locked settings file.

BOTH-SUBSCRIPTION-HARD-CANCEL.title: Canceling needs a call, letter or visit
BOTH-SUBSCRIPTION-HARD-CANCEL.problem:
Your app makes canceling much harder than signing up.
- Signing up takes one tap.
- Canceling needs a phone call, letter or visit.
- This covers plans billed outside Apple's or Google's payments.
- A US national cancel rule was struck down in 2025.
- California, New York and Massachusetts still have their own laws.
- The US trade agency (FTC) can still act anyway.
BOTH-SUBSCRIPTION-HARD-CANCEL.fix:
For plans billed outside the stores, let people cancel themselves.
- Add a cancel button in your app.
- Or add one on an account settings web page.
- Make it at least as easy as signing up.
- Never make people call, write or visit to cancel.

BOTH-UNREACHABLE-METADATA-URL.title: Broken links on your store page
BOTH-UNREACHABLE-METADATA-URL.problem:
A support, marketing or privacy policy link on your store page doesn't load.
A common checking tool (fastlane precheck) flags this too.
BOTH-UNREACHABLE-METADATA-URL.fix:
Check every link on your store page.
- Each one must be public.
- Each one must load for the whole review time.

BOTH-UNSAFE-DEEPLINK.title: Unsafe app links used for private actions
BOTH-UNSAFE-DEEPLINK.problem:
Your app uses its own custom link type for private actions.
These include sending people to screens or passing login keys.
Your app doesn't strictly check what comes in through those links.
BOTH-UNSAFE-DEEPLINK.fix:
Use links tied to your own website instead.
- On iPhone, use Apple's website links (Universal Links).
- On Android, use Android's verified website links.
- Clean up every value that arrives through a link.

BOTH-WITHDRAWAL-BUTTON-MISSING.title: No clear withdraw button for EU users
BOTH-WITHDRAWAL-BUTTON-MISSING.problem:
Your app sells subscriptions or online contracts to people in the EU.
It has no clear, easy to find withdraw button or option.
EU law says people can back out within 14 days.
BOTH-WITHDRAWAL-BUTTON-MISSING.fix:
Add a clear withdraw button or option to your app's screens.
- Make it easy to find.
- Give it its own spot.
- Let people back out without extra hassle.

CHINA-AI-REFERENCES.title: Outside AI services named in China store
CHINA-AI-REFERENCES.problem:
Your app in the China App Store mentions outside AI services.
- Examples are ChatGPT, Gemini and OpenAI.
- This can get your app turned down in China.
- A person checks this by hand.
CHINA-AI-REFERENCES.fix: Remove or change mentions of outside AI services in your China version.

FLUTTER-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.title: Flutter add-ons used without Apple's privacy file
FLUTTER-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.problem:
Your Flutter app has no Apple privacy file anywhere.
Yet it uses add-ons that touch phone features Apple watches, such as:
- permissions, photo picking or location
- device or app info
- saved settings or local databases
- Firebase
FLUTTER-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.fix:
Add Apple's privacy file (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) for the whole app.
- Check each Flutter add-on ships its own file.
- Most do from Flutter 3.19 on.
- If one lacks a file, Apple can't see its reasons.
- Apple only sees them if your app's file lists them.

GOOGLE-12-TESTER-RULE.title: New personal account skipped the closed test
GOOGLE-12-TESTER-RULE.problem:
Your new personal developer account hasn't finished closed testing.
Google needs at least 12 testers for 14 days in a row.
This must happen before you can go live.
GOOGLE-12-TESTER-RULE.fix:
Run a closed test with at least 12 testers.
- Keep it going for 14 days in a row.
- Or use a company account, if that fits you.

GOOGLE-DATASAFETY-MISMATCH.title: Data safety form doesn't match your app
GOOGLE-DATASAFETY-MISMATCH.problem:
Add-on code for stats, ads or tracking collects or shares data.
Your Data safety form doesn't list it.
This is Google's top reason for turning apps down.
GOOGLE-DATASAFETY-MISMATCH.fix:
Check every add-on and every way data moves while your app runs.
- List all data you collect.
- List all data you share.
- Describe how you protect it.
- Make every answer in the form correct.

GOOGLE-FAMILIES-AD-SDK.title: Wrong ad code in a kids app
GOOGLE-FAMILIES-AD-SDK.problem:
Your app is listed as made for children.
It uses ad add-on code Google hasn't approved for families.
Or it shows kids ads based on what they do.
GOOGLE-FAMILIES-AD-SDK.fix:
Use only ad add-on code Google approves for families (Families certified).
Stop showing kids ads based on what they do.

GOOGLE-MISLEADING-LISTING.title: Store page promises features the app lacks
GOOGLE-MISLEADING-LISTING.problem:
A reviewer checks your store page by hand.
The text, screenshots and description must match what your app really does.
GOOGLE-MISLEADING-LISTING.fix:
Make your store page match your app exactly.
Use screenshots of real screens from your app.

GOOGLE-MISSING-PRIVACY-POLICY.title: No privacy policy link
GOOGLE-MISSING-PRIVACY-POLICY.problem:
Your app collects user data.
Your store page in Play Console has no privacy policy link.
GOOGLE-MISSING-PRIVACY-POLICY.fix:
Publish a privacy policy online.
Then add its web address to your store page in Play Console.

GOOGLE-PERM-ACCESSIBILITY-MISUSE.title: Accessibility tools used for other things
GOOGLE-PERM-ACCESSIBILITY-MISUSE.problem:
Your app asks to act as an accessibility tool (BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE).
But your app isn't an accessibility tool.
GOOGLE-PERM-ACCESSIBILITY-MISUSE.fix:
Only use accessibility features for real accessibility needs.
Tell Google how your app uses them.
Otherwise, remove the accessibility tool from your app.

GOOGLE-PERM-ALL-FILES.title: Asks to see all files without reason
GOOGLE-PERM-ALL-FILES.problem:
Your app asks to see every file on the phone (MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE).
Google allows this only for certain uses that qualify.
GOOGLE-PERM-ALL-FILES.fix:
Use limited file access instead (scoped storage).
Ask to see all files only if your use qualifies.
If it does, send Google the required form.

GOOGLE-PERM-BACKGROUND-LOCATION.title: Background location without a main feature
GOOGLE-PERM-BACKGROUND-LOCATION.problem:
Your app asks for location while it isn't in use (ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION).
It has no clear main feature that needs this.
Or it shows users no clear notice about it.
GOOGLE-PERM-BACKGROUND-LOCATION.fix:
Ask for location only while your app is in use, if you can.
If you need it in the background, you must:
- Have a main feature that needs it.
- Show users a clear, easy to see notice.
- Fill in Google's permission form.

GOOGLE-PERM-SMS-CALLLOG.title: Text or call log access without approval
GOOGLE-PERM-SMS-CALLLOG.problem:
Your app asks for texts or call history without an approved main use.
- Texts: reading, sending or getting them.
- Call history: reading or changing it.
- From 26 August 2026, phone call account checks stop qualifying (READ_CALL_LOG).
GOOGLE-PERM-SMS-CALLLOG.fix:
Fill in Google's permission form for an approved main use.
Or remove the permission.
To check accounts, use one of these instead:
- Digital Credentials API
- SMS Retriever API

GOOGLE-PLAY-AGE-SIGNALS-MISUSE.title: Age signals used for ads or tracking
GOOGLE-PLAY-AGE-SIGNALS-MISUSE.problem:
Your app uses Google's age signals tool (Play Age Signals API).
It also has add-on code for ads, marketing, user profiles or usage tracking.
This breaks Google Play's strict terms.
GOOGLE-PLAY-AGE-SIGNALS-MISUSE.fix:
Use age signals only to show content and experiences that fit the user's age.
This use must follow the law.
Never use the tool or its answers for:
- ads
- marketing
- building profiles of users
- tracking how people use your app

GOOGLE-PLAY-BILLING.title: Digital items sold without Google's payment system
GOOGLE-PLAY-BILLING.problem:
Your app sells digital items with a web checkout or payment add-on.
Google wants its own payment system used for these (Play Billing).
GOOGLE-PLAY-BILLING.fix:
Use Google's payment system for digital items sold in your app.
Use other options only in regions where Google allows them.

GOOGLE-TARGET-API.title: App aims at an old Android version
GOOGLE-TARGET-API.problem:
Your app aims at an older Android version than Google Play requires (targetSdkVersion).
- New apps and updates from 31 August 2026: API 36 or higher.
- Play Console can give you until 1 November 2026.
- Wear OS and Automotive OS apps: API 35 or higher.
- TV and XR apps: API 34 or higher.
GOOGLE-TARGET-API.fix:
Ask your developer to raise the target Android version.
From 31 August 2026, that means API 36 (Android 16) or higher.
Google Play rejects lower versions automatically.

GOOGLE-PLAY-BILLING-V8-REQUIRED.title: Google payment code older than version 8
GOOGLE-PLAY-BILLING-V8-REQUIRED.problem:
Your app uses Google's payment add-on code (Play Billing Library) below version 8.
- From 31 August 2026, new apps and updates need version 8 or later.
- A Play Console extension is available until 1 November 2026.
- Apps already live on version 7 can keep taking payments.
- That lasts until the 2027 deadline for all apps.
GOOGLE-PLAY-BILLING-V8-REQUIRED.fix:
Ask your developer to upgrade to version 8 (com.android.billingclient:billing 8.x).
Or ask for the extension in Play Console before 1 November 2026.

IONIC-4.2-THIN-WRAPPER.title: Website in an app shell, little else
IONIC-4.2-THIN-WRAPPER.problem:
Your app is mostly a website in an app shell (Capacitor, Cordova or WKWebView).
It uses fewer than 2 native phone features from this list:
- status bar, splash screen, push alerts
- vibration, share, camera, local alerts
Apple wants features, content or design beyond a repackaged website.
This check is only a rough guess.
A person reviews it before calling it a blocker.
IONIC-4.2-THIN-WRAPPER.fix:
This is the most common reason Ionic apps get turned down.
Add native add-ons for these:
- status bar
- splash screen transition
- push alerts
- phone vibration
Or ship it as an installable web app (PWA).
That skips App Review.

IONIC-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.title: Plugins without Apple's privacy file
IONIC-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.problem:
Your app uses Capacitor or Cordova plugins.
No Apple privacy file (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) exists anywhere in your project.
Some plugins wrap native add-on code that needs this file.
IONIC-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.fix:
Plugin support for this file is less standard than Flutter's.
- Add one privacy file for your whole app.
- Check each plugin that wraps native add-on code.
- Examples are camera, location and ads plugins.
- Each of those must ship its own privacy file.

IONIC-UIWEBVIEW-DEPRECATED.title: Uses Apple's retired web viewer
IONIC-UIWEBVIEW-DEPRECATED.problem:
Your built code still contains Apple's retired web viewer (UIWebView).
Often an old Capacitor or Cordova plugin pulls it in.
Apple automatically rejects any app with it built in, error ITMS-90809.
IONIC-UIWEBVIEW-DEPRECATED.fix: Update every plugin to a version using the newer web viewer (WKWebView).

RN-OTA-UNDECLARED.title: Hidden live updates to your app's code
RN-OTA-UNDECLARED.problem:
Your app can change its code after Apple approves it.
- It uses React Native or Expo.
- It has a live updater, such as react-native-code-push.
- Others are expo-updates, react-native-ota-hot-update and Stallion.
- Your App Review notes don't say it's for bug fixes only.
RN-OTA-UNDECLARED.fix:
Be open about the updater and limit what it does.
- Name the live update tool in your App Review notes.
- Use it only for bug fixes.
- Don't change purpose, screens or features beyond what Apple reviewed.
- Since 16 October 2026, Apple calls hidden feature updates bait and switch.

RN-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.title: React Native app missing Apple's privacy file
RN-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.problem:
Your React Native or Expo app has no Apple privacy file (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy).
Some of its native parts use phone features Apple watches.
Examples are Firebase, AsyncStorage and expo-file-system.
RN-PRIVACY-MANIFEST-MISSING.fix:
Add one privacy file for your whole app.
Some native parts come in through your other packages.
Each of those needs its own file, combined in the final app file.

WEB-COOKIE-CONSENT.title: Setting extra cookies before users agree
WEB-COOKIE-CONSENT.problem:
Your site saves cookies in code (document.cookie or cookieStore).
It doesn't first check that the user said yes in a cookie banner.
EU privacy law needs a clear yes for cookies that aren't essential.
WEB-COOKIE-CONSENT.fix:
Add a cookie banner that follows the rules.
It must block non-essential cookies until the user clearly says yes.

WEB-GDPR-COMPLIANCE.title: Collecting personal data without privacy controls
WEB-GDPR-COMPLIANCE.problem:
Your site handles personal data but lacks one of these:
- a clear opt-in before using the data
- a link to your privacy policy
- a way for users to delete their data
WEB-GDPR-COMPLIANCE.fix:
Add standard privacy steps to your site, including:
- a clear opt-in before you use personal data
- a way for users to delete their data

WEB-INDEXEDDB.title: Unprotected personal data in browser database
WEB-INDEXEDDB.problem:
Your site keeps user records in the browser's database (IndexedDB).
It does this without consent, encryption or a plan to delete them.
WEB-INDEXEDDB.fix:
Protect these records:
- Store sensitive records through an encrypted helper.
- Check the user's consent first.
- Clear the database when the user logs out.

WEB-LOCAL-STORAGE.title: Plain text sensitive data in browser storage
WEB-LOCAL-STORAGE.problem:
Your site saves sensitive details or login tokens in browser storage (localStorage).
They're in plain text, not encrypted.
Or the site doesn't check the user's consent first.
WEB-LOCAL-STORAGE.fix:
Don't keep sensitive personal details there in plain text.
- Encrypt any tokens you store.
- Respect the user's storage choices.

WEB-SESSION-STORAGE.title: Unprotected login keys in tab storage
WEB-SESSION-STORAGE.problem:
Your site saves raw login or session keys in tab storage (sessionStorage).
They aren't encrypted, or nothing clears them later.
WEB-SESSION-STORAGE.fix:
Protect what you save there:
- Save as little as you can.
- Encrypt what you save.
- Delete it when the session ends.

WEB-TRACKING-TECHNOLOGIES.title: Tracking code loads before visitors agree
WEB-TRACKING-TECHNOLOGIES.problem:
Your site loads tracking code from other companies before visitors say yes.
Examples are Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel and Hotjar.
EU privacy law needs clear consent first.
WEB-TRACKING-TECHNOLOGIES.fix:
Load tracking scripts and pixels only after a visitor agrees to cookies.
The visitor must say yes clearly.

BOTH-US-ASAA-AGE-SIGNALS-MISSING.title: Missing store age signals for US laws
BOTH-US-ASAA-AGE-SIGNALS-MISSING.problem:
Your app may break US state age laws, like Utah's and Texas's.
- It has accounts or features locked by age.
- It doesn't use store age signals (Declared Age Range, Play Age Signals API).
- It has no proven parent consent for children's accounts.
- Utah's duties for the stores began 6 May 2026.
- This is a rough guess, not legal proof.
BOTH-US-ASAA-AGE-SIGNALS-MISSING.fix:
Ask your developer to make these changes.
- Use the store age signals.
- Get proven parent consent before a child uses an account.
- Ask for consent again after big changes.
- Delete raw age check data once the check is done.

GOOGLE-PAYMENTS-DONATION-LINK.title: Donation link that skips Google Play billing
GOOGLE-PAYMENTS-DONATION-LINK.problem:
Your app links to donations outside Play billing.
Think Open Collective, Ko-fi, Patreon, Buy Me a Coffee or GitHub Sponsors.
Liberapay and PayPal donate pages count too.
Only tax exempt charities may skip it, not trade groups or informal projects.
Everything else counts as paying for digital goods.
Open source apps get hit most, like AnkiDroid in August 2026.
GOOGLE-PAYMENTS-DONATION-LINK.fix:
Pick one of these:
- Remove the donation link from your Play version.
- Sell it through Play billing as a one time purchase.
- For a tax exempt charity, add proof to review notes.
A separate Play build is enough to remove it (build flavor).
Don't argue in your appeal. Google already said trade groups don't qualify.

APPLE-2.3.6-SOCIAL-MEDIA-DECLARATION.title: Social media question left unanswered
APPLE-2.3.6-SOCIAL-MEDIA-DECLARATION.problem:
Since September 2026, Apple asks if your app has social media features.
- You must answer for every new version and update.
- You must also answer for apps in other app stores.
- Social features include feeds, followers, chat rooms and direct messages.
- Live streams count too.
- Without an answer, you can't submit.
APPLE-2.3.6-SOCIAL-MEDIA-DECLARATION.fix:
Answer the social media question in App Store Connect.
- Your developer can also set it with Apple's upload tools.
- Saying yes puts your app in the social media time limit group.
- Your app's age rating becomes at least 13+.
- Under 13 users need Apple's age range tool (Declared Age Range API).

APPLE-4.0-SIWA-RELAY-DOMAIN.title: New Hide My Email addresses get rejected
APPLE-4.0-SIWA-RELAY-DOMAIN.problem:
Your app only accepts Hide My Email addresses on privaterelay.appleid.com.
Apple now also uses private.icloud.com, so those sign-ups fail quietly.
Apple rejects apps with a broken Sign in with Apple.
APPLE-4.0-SIWA-RELAY-DOMAIN.fix:
Accept both privaterelay.appleid.com and private.icloud.com.
Do this everywhere you check, allow or match email addresses.
Change it on your servers and in the app.

APPLE-5.1.1-RESCIND-CONSENT-UNHANDLED.title: App ignores a parent taking back consent
APPLE-5.1.1-RESCIND-CONSENT-UNHANDLED.problem:
Your app reads Apple's Declared Age Range but ignores one alert.
- It's the alert that a parent withdrew consent (RESCIND_CONSENT).
- Then Apple stops your app from opening.
- But the child's data on your servers stays.
- So does any access tied to that consent.
APPLE-5.1.1-RESCIND-CONSENT-UNHANDLED.fix:
Ask your developer to make these changes.
- Sign up for Apple's App Store server alerts.
- When consent is withdrawn, sign the child out.
- Delete the data tied to that consent.
- Build with the iOS 26.2 kit and Xcode 26.2 (17C52) or later.
- Apple requires this for all its age check tools.

APPLE-3.1.1-EXTERNAL-LINK-REGION-GATING.title: Outside purchase link shown in every country
APPLE-3.1.1-EXTERNAL-LINK-REGION-GATING.problem:
Your app shows an outside purchase link everywhere.
Only the US store allows this without permission from Apple.
Japan, Canada, Australia, the UK and most others don't.
Apple reviews each region separately.
Since 16 October 2026, music streaming apps share this permission.
Links must go to allowed places, which vary by region.
Developers expect two rejections from this in 2026.
APPLE-3.1.1-EXTERNAL-LINK-REGION-GATING.fix:
Show the link only where it's allowed.
- Check the app's current store country (Storefront.current countryCode).
- Show it where you have Apple's permission.
- Or show it in the US store.
Outside the US, keep the permission route and Apple's notice screen.

APPLE-4.5.3-LIVE-ACTIVITY-SPAM.title: Live Activities used for ads or spam
APPLE-4.5.3-LIVE-ACTIVITY-SPAM.problem:
Your app's Live Activities show ads, offers or unrelated content.
Since 8 June 2026, Apple bans spam, scams and unwanted messages there.
The same ban already covered Game Center and push notifications.
APPLE-4.5.3-LIVE-ACTIVITY-SPAM.fix:
Tie every Live Activity to a real, timed task the user started.
- No ads or offers to buy more.
- No bait to make people open the app.
- Nothing unrelated on the Lock Screen or in the Dynamic Island.

APPLE-ODR-DEPRECATED-27.title: Still using On-Demand Resources
APPLE-ODR-DEPRECATED-27.problem:
Apple is phasing out On-Demand Resources, starting in iOS 27.
- This also covers iPadOS 27, tvOS 27 and visionOS 27.
- Apps using its tagged downloads (NSBundleResourceRequest) will lose them later.
- From early 2027, new apps can't upload files that use it.
- Nor can apps that have never used it.
- Apple said this on 12 November 2026.
APPLE-ODR-DEPRECATED-27.fix:
Move tagged files to Apple's Background Assets tool.
Do it before iOS 27 and its family become the minimum for submissions.

APPLE-ASCAPI-AGERATING-ENDPOINT-REMOVED.title: Removed age rating request breaks your release
APPLE-ASCAPI-AGERATING-ENDPOINT-REMOVED.problem:
Apple removed two ways to read your app's age rating in App Store Connect.
Your release tools may still use them (fastlane, scripts, CI).
If so, they fail and your release stops.
APPLE-ASCAPI-AGERATING-ENDPOINT-REMOVED.fix:
Ask your developer to switch to Apple's current age rating requests.
- Use the current ones for reading and updating.
- If your app has social features, set the social media fields.
- Test the tools on a TestFlight build before your next release.

APPLE-MACOS-ROSETTA-SUNSET.title: Mac app that only runs on Intel
APPLE-MACOS-ROSETTA-SUNSET.problem:
Your Mac app only runs on Intel chips.
Apple's two notices disagree on when that stops working.
- 1 September 2026: macOS 27 is the last with Rosetta.
- After it, Intel only apps stop running on Apple chips.
- 9 September 2026: macOS 26 is last for Intel Macs and Rosetta.
- That notice says macOS 27 runs on Apple chips only.
APPLE-MACOS-ROSETTA-SUNSET.fix:
Plan for the earlier date.
Your app must run directly on Apple chips before macOS 27 ships.
- Ship a universal or Apple chip build (arm64).
- Replace add-on code that only runs on Intel.
- Test on an Apple chip Mac without Rosetta installed.
- Check by hand which chips your builds and add-ons support.

GOOGLE-ORG-REGISTRATION-REQUIRED.title: Regulated app published from a personal account
GOOGLE-ORG-REGISTRATION-REQUIRED.problem:
From 30 September 2026, some apps need an organization account.
- Money apps: banking, loans, trading, investment funds, crypto wallets and exchanges.
- Health apps: medical, or research on people.
- Apps approved to use Android's VPN feature (VpnService).
- Government apps.
The account needs a D-U-N-S number matching its Dun and Bradstreet profile.
GOOGLE-ORG-REGISTRATION-REQUIRED.fix:
Move the app to an organization account before 30 September 2026.
- Turn your account into one, or create a new one.
- Get a D-U-N-S number.
- Keep account details the same as your Dun and Bradstreet profile.
- Use Google's official Transfer ownership steps to move the app.

GOOGLE-PLAY-APP-REGISTRATION-MISSING.title: App not registered for Google developer verification
GOOGLE-PLAY-APP-REGISTRATION-MISSING.problem:
Google requires this for Android developer verification.
- Each app ID (package name) must be registered in Play Console.
- The deadline is 30 September 2026.
- This applies in every country.
- Unregistered apps may be removed from Google Play worldwide.
GOOGLE-PLAY-APP-REGISTRATION-MISSING.fix:
Open Play Console and check by hand.
- Finish developer verification.
- Register every app ID you share with users.
- Test builds you never share don't need it.
- Check again after adding a new app ID or app variant.

GOOGLE-CONTACTS-PICKER-REQUIRED.title: Full contacts access when a picker works
GOOGLE-CONTACTS-PICKER-REQUIRED.problem:
Your app asks to read all the user's contacts (READ_CONTACTS).
This applies if your app is built for Android 17 or later.
- Ask only if Android's contact picker can't do the main job.
- You must also fill in a form in Play Console.
- Checks before review start 27 October 2026.
- Full enforcement starts 27 January 2027.
GOOGLE-CONTACTS-PICKER-REQUIRED.fix:
Use Android's contact picker for one-off choices.
- Keep full access only for a real core need.
- Examples are a phone dialer or contacts manager.
- If you keep it, fill in the Play Console form.

GOOGLE-LOCATION-BUTTON-SCOPE.title: Location asked without Android's location button
GOOGLE-LOCATION-BUTTON-SCOPE.problem:
Your app asks for broad location access (ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION) for a tap-to-locate feature.
From 27 January 2027, this breaks the rules if:
- Your app is built for Android 17 or later.
- Location is only needed when the user taps something.
GOOGLE-LOCATION-BUTTON-SCOPE.fix:
Use Android's location button for one-time location.
- Turn on the button-only setting (onlyForLocationButton) in your app's settings file.
- Keep broad location access only for ongoing features that need it.

GOOGLE-FGS-GEOFENCE-REMOVED.title: Location service kept running just for geofences
GOOGLE-FGS-GEOFENCE-REMOVED.problem:
Your app runs a location service with a constant notice, just for geofences.
Geofences tell your app when someone enters or leaves an area.
Apps built for Android 17 (API 37) can't use that service for this.
From 27 January 2027, Google Play rejects these apps.
GOOGLE-FGS-GEOFENCE-REMOVED.fix:
Switch to Android's geofence tool (GeofencingClient).
If geofences were its only use, drop the location service permission.

ANDROID-LOCAL-NETWORK-PERMISSION.title: Local network use without asking permission
ANDROID-LOCAL-NETWORK-PERMISSION.problem:
Your app uses the local network without asking permission first.
From Android 17, the rule applies to apps built for API 37 or later.
These then fail with a security error:
- Searching for devices on the network.
- Sending one message to many devices at once.
- Connecting directly to devices on the network.
ANDROID-LOCAL-NETWORK-PERMISSION.fix:
Ask your developer to add the local network permission (ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK).
- Ask the user for it before searching or connecting on the network.
- Keep the app working as well as it can if refused.

ANDROID-R8-OPTIMIZATION-MISSING.title: Release build not optimized, shrunk or scrambled
ANDROID-R8-OPTIMIZATION-MISSING.problem:
From February 2027, apps must be optimized with a tool like R8.
At least 25 percent coverage is needed across three steps:
- Optimizing the code.
- Shrinking the app.
- Scrambling the code so it's hard to read.
A release build with shrinking off, or never set, falls short.
Those apps get less visibility and lose publishing abilities.
ANDROID-R8-OPTIMIZATION-MISSING.fix:
Turn on R8 in your release build before February 2027.
- Turn on code and resource shrinking (isMinifyEnabled, isShrinkResources).
- Fix the rules for code R8 must keep.
- Check the optimization report in Play Console.

ANDROID-RESTORE-CREDENTIALS-REQUIRED.title: Sign-in not carried over to new devices
ANDROID-RESTORE-CREDENTIALS-REQUIRED.problem:
From April 2027, Google Play has a new sign-in rule.
- It covers any app with sign-in, optional or required.
- Moving to a new Android device must keep users signed in.
- Your app must do this with the Restore Credentials API.
- Games are left out for now.
- Sign-in without this setup misses the rule.
ANDROID-RESTORE-CREDENTIALS-REQUIRED.fix:
Ask your developer to use Google's Credential Manager for three steps.
- Create a restore key (restore credential) when someone signs in.
- Restore it the first time your app opens after the move.
- Clear it when someone signs out.

GOOGLE-GENAI-NCII-CONTROLS.title: AI images of people without safety checks
GOOGLE-GENAI-NCII-CONTROLS.problem:
Your app makes or edits images or video of people.
Google requires all of these:
- Content checks built for your app, on requests and results.
- A written record of safety prompts and tricky cases tested.
- A test account with full, free access to every AI feature.
Suspended apps can't make money or advertise anywhere on Google.
GOOGLE-GENAI-NCII-CONTROLS.fix:
You need all three.
- Block intimate and fake real-person content (deepfakes) going in and out.
- Keep a written record of safety prompts and tricky cases tested.
- Put a full-access test account in Play Console review notes.

GOOGLE-ANON-CHAT-MINOR-BLOCK.title: Stranger chat app that doesn't block children
GOOGLE-ANON-CHAT-MINOR-BLOCK.problem:
Your app mainly connects strangers at random, or lets people chat with hidden identities.
From 26 August 2026, Google requires these apps to:
- Block minors with Play Console tools.
- Never aim at children.
- Follow its child safety rules, including removing child sexual abuse material.
GOOGLE-ANON-CHAT-MINOR-BLOCK.fix:
Make these changes:
- Turn on the Play Console tools that block minors.
- Set age rating and audience to exclude children.
- Publish your standards against child sexual exploitation and abuse (CSAE).
- Add a way to report problems inside the app.
- Name a contact for child safety.

GOOGLE-UNRATED-APP-BANNED.title: App with no content rating
GOOGLE-UNRATED-APP-BANNED.problem:
Google doesn't allow apps with no content rating.
- An unfinished rating form blocks publishing.
- So does an expired one (IARC questionnaire).
- Check it yourself in Play Console.
GOOGLE-UNRATED-APP-BANNED.fix:
Fill in the content rating form for every app.
Answer it again whenever features change, such as:
- Chat.
- Content users post.
- Gambling.
- AI-made content.

APPLE-ENROLLMENT-VERIFICATION-PENDING.title: Launch set before developer account is active
APPLE-ENROLLMENT-VERIFICATION-PENDING.problem:
It's not a rejection. It blocks you before review.
Accounts can sit in Pending two to six weeks after payment.
Developers also report:
- ID upload links failing with an access error.
- No support reply for weeks.
- A personal to company switch open 61 days.
Launch dates assuming day one access slip by weeks.
APPLE-ENROLLMENT-VERIFICATION-PENDING.fix:
Check account, agreement and switch status before booking a date.
- Enroll and verify at least six weeks before first submission.
- Have government ID ready.
- Accept each agreement update and attachment promptly.
- Brazil's due 6 July 2026, EU's before 1 October 2026.
- Start any personal to company switch three months ahead.
- Track your case number. Phone support, not just email.

APPLE-2.3.14-CREATIVE-ASSET-CONTENT.title: Store artwork with prices or misleading claims
APPLE-2.3.14-CREATIVE-ASSET-CONTENT.problem:
Since 16 October 2026, a person checks your store page header and search art.
Yours shows one of these:
- Specific or discounted prices.
- A claim about the app nobody can check.
- Another app, mentioned to mislead.
- Content not right for all ages.
- Art unrelated to your app's content, features or brand.
APPLE-2.3.14-CREATIVE-ASSET-CONTENT.fix:
Follow Apple's artwork guidelines.
- Show only your app or its brand.
- Make it right for all ages.
- No prices, discounts or rankings.
- No claims nobody can check.
- No mentions of other apps.

APPLE-2.5.19-HIDDEN-OR-DORMANT-FEATURE.title: Hidden features or a switch after review
APPLE-2.5.19-HIDDEN-OR-DORMANT-FEATURE.problem:
Your app has features the reviewer can't see or users aren't told about.
- A server switch turns on a different app after approval.
- A secret gesture or menu.
- Code scrambled to hide a feature.
- Since 16 October 2026, Apple's rule names this bait and switch.
- It means misleading review, then adding features after approval.
- A person checks this. A remote switch alone is allowed.
APPLE-2.5.19-HIDDEN-OR-DORMANT-FEATURE.fix:
Show the reviewer everything your app does.
- Make every feature visible during review.
- Describe each feature in Notes for Review.
- Remote settings may only tune or gradually release reviewed features.
- Never scramble code to hide a feature.
- Breaking this can get your app removed.
- It can also end your developer account.

APPLE-5-TRAFFICKING-CHILD-EXPLOITATION.title: Helping human trafficking or child exploitation
APPLE-5-TRAFFICKING-CHILD-EXPLOITATION.problem:
Since 16 October 2026, apps that help trafficking or child exploitation face this.
- Apple reports them to the authorities.
- Apple removes them from the App Store.
- Apple blocks them from other app stores too.
- Risky apps include marketplaces and classified ads.
- Also escort or companion listings.
- Also apps with anonymous contact.
- Also any place where adults can reach kids or teens.
- A person checks this.
APPLE-5-TRAFFICKING-CHILD-EXPLOITATION.fix:
Protect your app against these harms.
- Check listings and messages for signs of trafficking or child exploitation.
- Verify ages wherever adults can reach kids or teens.
- Report child sexual abuse material to NCMEC, as US law requires.
- Keep the reporting tools required for user content.

APPLE-MIN-DEPLOYMENT-TARGET-IOS13.title: Oldest supported iOS is below 13
APPLE-MIN-DEPLOYMENT-TARGET-IOS13.problem:
Your app's lowest supported iOS is below 13. Apple refuses the upload.
- This covers iPhone and iPad apps.
- Your project setting or add-on list (Podfile) can cause this.
- An add-on or test part below 13 alone won't block upload.
- So the checker marks that as high risk, not blocking.
APPLE-MIN-DEPLOYMENT-TARGET-IOS13.fix:
Ask your developer to set the lowest iOS to 13.0 or later.
Change it in three places:
- The project.
- The app target.
- The add-on list (Podfile).

APPLE-2.5.5-IPV4-ONLY-NETWORKING.title: App breaks on Apple's IPv6-only test network
APPLE-2.5.5-IPV4-ONLY-NETWORKING.problem:
Reviewers test on a network that only uses IPv6.
Some older network code only works with IPv4 (inet_addr, inet_aton, gethostbyname).
So your app looks broken in review, and apps must fully work on IPv6.
APPLE-2.5.5-IPV4-ONLY-NETWORKING.fix:
Ask your developer to switch to current network tools.
- Use newer options (getaddrinfo, Network.framework or URLSession).
- Don't type IPv4 addresses straight into the code.
- Test on an IPv6-only network, using Mac Internet Sharing.

APPLE-5.1.3-HEALTH-DATA-ICLOUD.title: Health data might end up in iCloud
APPLE-5.1.3-HEALTH-DATA-ICLOUD.problem:
Apple bans storing personal health data in iCloud.
Your app reads Apple Health data (HealthKit) and also syncs to iCloud.
Someone must check health data never goes that way.
APPLE-5.1.3-HEALTH-DATA-ICLOUD.fix:
Keep all health data on the phone or a server you control.
Leave it out of every iCloud sync (CloudKit, NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore, NSPersistentCloudKitContainer).

ANDROID-DEBUGGABLE-RELEASE.title: Test build uploaded to Google Play
ANDROID-DEBUGGABLE-RELEASE.problem:
Your app upload is marked as a debugging build.
Google Play refuses any upload marked this way.
This happens when the setting is written straight into the app's settings file.
ANDROID-DEBUGGABLE-RELEASE.fix:
Ask your developer to remove the debugging setting (android:debuggable) from the settings file.
The release build then keeps it switched off by itself.

ANDROID-FGS-SPECIAL-USE-UNDECLARED.title: Special ongoing task with no stated reason
ANDROID-FGS-SPECIAL-USE-UNDECLARED.problem:
Your app runs an ongoing task marked special use (specialUse foreground service).
Google asks why and can reject your update unless you have:
- A label naming its purpose, inside the task
- A written reason in the Play Console form
ANDROID-FGS-SPECIAL-USE-UNDECLARED.fix:
Ask your developer to add the purpose label inside the task (PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE).
Then fill in the ongoing task form in Play Console.
Or switch the task to a more specific type instead.

ANDROID-64BIT-ABI-MISSING.title: Missing a 64-bit version of built-in code
ANDROID-64BIT-ABI-MISSING.problem:
Google Play needs a 64-bit copy of every low-level code library.
Your app's chip list (abiFilters) has 32-bit Arm but not 64-bit Arm.
That fails the rule.
ANDROID-64BIT-ABI-MISSING.fix:
Add these to the chip list (abiFilters):
- arm64-v8a, for 64-bit Arm phones
- x86_64, if your app also ships x86

EU-AI-ACT-ART-4.title: Train your team to understand AI
EU-AI-ACT-ART-4.summary:
This applies if you make an AI system or use one.
Your team must know enough about AI for how you use it.
A written policy, onboarding and log help prove it, but aren't required.

EU-AI-ACT-ART-5.title: Some uses of AI are banned
EU-AI-ACT-ART-5.summary:
Your app must not use AI in banned ways. These include:
- Hidden tricks that steer people without them noticing.
- Taking advantage of children.
- Giving people scores based on how they behave.
- Sorting people into groups using face or body data.

EU-AI-ACT-ART-50.title: Tell people when AI is involved
EU-AI-ACT-ART-50.summary:
Your app must be open about AI:
- Tell people when they're talking to an AI.
- Mark content that AI made.
- Label fake but real looking photos, videos or audio as AI made.

EU-AI-ACT-GPAI.title: Rules for general purpose AI models start
EU-AI-ACT-GPAI.summary:
If you provide a general purpose AI model, you must meet its rules.
The AI law's rules on oversight and fines also start to apply.

EU-AI-ACT-HIGH-RISK-ANNEX-III.title: High-risk AI rules start later
EU-AI-ACT-HIGH-RISK-ANNEX-III.summary:
Rules for high-risk AI (Annex III) now start later. The delay is final, not a proposal. It was set on 8 July 2026 and took effect 27 July 2026. The delayed rules cover:
- What you must do.
- Checks that you follow the rules.
- How you oversee and run your AI.

EU-AI-ACT-HIGH-RISK-ANNEX-I.title: High risk AI inside physical products
EU-AI-ACT-HIGH-RISK-ANNEX-I.summary: This covers AI built into things like machines, toys and lifts. It must meet the high risk AI rules. A rule change in force since 27 July 2026 delayed this date. It was set on 8 July 2026 and is final.

EU-DMA-EXTERNAL-PURCHASE.title: Rules for outside payments and offers
EU-DMA-EXTERNAL-PURCHASE.summary:
If you offer other ways to pay or link to outside offers:
- Get permission from Apple (External Purchases or Offers Entitlement).
- Show Apple's notice screen for your link.
- Show Apple's in-app purchase just as clearly, if offered.
- Add a parent check for kids.
- Keep the options for 12 months.
- Report sales every month.

EU-DSA-TRADER-STATUS.title: Declare trader status or leave EU store
EU-DSA-TRADER-STATUS.summary:
Tell Apple if you're a trader. If you are, you must be verified:
- Your D-U-N-S number.
- Your phone and email, which get published.
- Two-step sign in, checked.
If you don't declare, or aren't verified, your app leaves the EU store.

EU-EAA-ACCESSIBILITY.title: Make your app accessible
EU-EAA-ACCESSIBILITY.summary:
Your app must be usable by people with disabilities. You must:
- Meet the EU mobile standard (EN 301 549 Chapter 11, WCAG 2.1 AA).
- Publish the required accessibility details.
- Put them in your terms or a similar document.

EU-DATA-ACT-CORE.title: Let users reach data from connected devices
EU-DATA-ACT-CORE.summary: This applies if your app works with connected products or wearables. Design it so users can get the data these create.

EU-DATA-ACT-DESIGN.title: Let users reach data from connected devices
EU-DATA-ACT-DESIGN.summary:
This applies to connected wearables and devices.
- Build them so users can reach their data.
- Build this in from the start.
- This rule is not about moving between cloud services.
- Cloud switching fees drop to zero on 12 January 2027.

EU-CRA-REPORTING.title: Report security flaws and incidents
EU-CRA-REPORTING.summary: You must report security flaws that attackers are actively using. You must also report security incidents.

EU-CRA-MAIN.title: Build security in and fix flaws
EU-CRA-MAIN.summary: Your app must be built to be secure from the start. You must also have a way to handle security flaws.

US-COPPA-AMENDED.title: Stricter rules for children's data
US-COPPA-AMENDED.summary:
If your app collects data from children:
- Treat face scans, fingerprints and similar data as personal data.
- Get a parent's separate OK to share data or show targeted ads.
- Write down how long you keep their data.
- Write a plan for keeping their data safe.
Two earlier dates exist: 90 days and 6 months after 22 April 2025. These apply only to FTC approved safe harbor groups, not app developers.

US-FTC-HEALTH-BREACH.title: Unapproved health data sharing counts as breach
US-FTC-HEALTH-BREACH.summary: Sharing health or sensitive data with advertisers without OK is a breach. If it happens, you must give notice within 60 days.

US-TX-ASAA.title: Check ages and get parent OK
US-TX-ASAA.summary:
It started 1 January 2026 and applies while an appeal goes on.
A court blocked it on 23 December 2025.
An appeals court paused that block on 4 June 2026.
The Supreme Court left that pause in place on 6 July 2026.
Your app must:
- Check ages and get a parent's proven OK for minors.
- Do this for downloads, purchases and major updates.
- Ask for the user's age group.
- Delete age data.

US-UT-ASAA.title: Get age group from the store
US-UT-ASAA.summary:
From 6 May 2027, your app must:
- Ask for and receive each user's age group from the store.
- Confirm a parent agreed for each minor's account.
- Delete age check data.
This now covers preinstalled apps too. Users can sue you for at least 1,000 dollars per violation. The state no longer writes extra rules or enforces it. A tech industry lawsuit against it was dropped on 21 April 2026.

US-LA-ASAA.title: Get age group and parents' OK
US-LA-ASAA.summary:
From 1 July 2027, your app must:
- Request an age group.
- Get a parent's OK.
- Ask for that OK again on major updates.
The 2025 version of this law never takes effect. Separately, Apple's store shares Louisiana age ranges on its own timeline.

US-AL-ASAA.title: App stores check ages and link parents
US-AL-ASAA.summary:
From 1 January 2027, app stores must:
- Check each user's age group.
- Link minors to a parent's account.
- Get a parent's verified OK for each download.
- Do the same for each in-app purchase.
- Accounts open on 2 October 2026 need an age check and consent.
- That must happen before 1 October 2027.

US-CA-CPRA.title: Honor privacy signals and opt-outs
US-CA-CPRA.summary:
Your app must:
- Respect the Global Privacy Control opt-out signal (GPC).
- Have a privacy policy.
- Give a notice when you collect data.
- Let people say no to selling, sharing or profiling their data.
- Follow limits on sensitive personal data.

US-IL-BIPA.title: Ask before collecting face or fingerprint data
US-IL-BIPA.summary:
If your app collects face scans, fingerprints or similar data:
- Tell people in writing first.
- Get their OK in writing before you collect.
- Publish how long you keep it.
- Delete it within 3 years.
- Never sell it.

UK-OSA-CHILD-SAFETY.title: Check user ages with methods that work
UK-OSA-CHILD-SAFETY.summary:
Your app must check ages with highly effective methods. This protects children from harmful content. Methods include:
- Estimating age from a face scan
- Checks through the user's bank (open banking)
- Credit card checks

UK-ICO-CHILDREN-CODE.title: Set strict privacy for children by default
UK-ICO-CHILDREN-CODE.summary:
If children may use your app:
- Set privacy to high by default.
- Collect only the data you need.
- Turn location off by default.
- Turn off building user profiles by default.
- Always do a written data risk check (DPIA).

AU-SOCIAL-MEDIA-MIN-AGE.title: Block under 16s from social media accounts
AU-SOCIAL-MEDIA-MIN-AGE.summary:
If your app is social media:
- Stop users under 16 from having accounts.
- Check ages with strong methods.
- Keep age check data walled off.
- Then destroy the age check data.

BR-DIGITAL-ECA.title: Check ages without a tick box
BR-DIGITAL-ECA.summary:
Your app must check users' ages:
- Check an ID document.
- Or estimate age from a face scan.
- Or check their tax ID number (CPF).
- Never rely on a tick box stating their age.

KR-TELECOM-BUSINESS-ACT.title: Rules for taking payments outside Apple
KR-TELECOM-BUSINESS-ACT.summary:
If your app takes payments outside Apple's system:
- Use only approved payment providers.
- Pay Apple a 26% fee.
- Get permission from Apple (com.apple.developer.storekit.external-purchase).
- Ship a separate app version only for South Korea.
- Show Apple's required notice screen.
- Send Apple the required reports.

IN-DPDPA-RULES.title: Get proven parent consent for under 18s
IN-DPDPA-RULES.summary:
If your app has users under 18:
- Get proof a parent agrees first.
- Use a government backed system, like DigiLocker.
- Don't track what they do.
- Don't show them targeted ads.

SG-IMDA-ONLINE-SAFETY.title: App stores must check user ages
SG-IMDA-ONLINE-SAFETY.summary: App stores must check users' ages and destroy that age data. They must block under 18s from apps unsuitable for their age. The wider rules for app stores began earlier, on 31 March 2025.

CN-MOBILE-APP-FILING.title: File your app with the government
CN-MOBILE-APP-FILING.summary:
To offer your app in China:
- File your app with the tech ministry (MIIT).
- Work with a local partner or company.
- Check users' real names.
- Follow China's privacy law.
- Keep user data inside China.
- Games also need a game license.

APPLE-AGE-RATING-QUESTIONNAIRE.title: Answer Apple's new age rating questions
APPLE-AGE-RATING-QUESTIONNAIRE.summary:
Every app must answer them, or it can't get updates. The questions cover:
- New ratings of 13+, 16+ and 18+
- Content your users post
- Live streaming

APPLE-XCODE-26-SDK-REQ.title: Build uploads with the version 26 kits
APPLE-XCODE-26-SDK-REQ.summary:
From 28 April 2026, build uploads with Apple's version 26 kits (SDK) or later:
- iOS 26 and iPadOS 26
- watchOS 26, tvOS 26 and visionOS 26
Mac apps are not on Apple's list. Age check features need the iOS 26.2 kit. They also need Xcode 26.2, build 17C52, or later.

APPLE-SDK-27-REQ.title: Build apps with Apple's version 27 tools
APPLE-SDK-27-REQ.summary:
Apps and games you upload from April 2027 need new build tools (SDK):
- iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 or later.
- Matching tvOS 27, visionOS 27 and watchOS 27.
- Mac apps aren't on Apple's list.
Apple hasn't named the day, so we track 1 April 2027. Check again when Apple names it. Apple announced this on 9 September 2026.

APPLE-IPHONE-DUO-SCREENSHOTS-REQ.title: Add iPhone Duo screenshots to submissions
APPLE-IPHONE-DUO-SCREENSHOTS-REQ.summary:
From April 2027, you need iPhone Duo screenshots to submit:
- Apple's screenshot rules say apps built with iOS 27.1 tools or later.
- Apple's 5 October 2026 news says every app and game.
- Apple has accepted Duo apps and screenshots since 5 October 2026.
- Store pages with them show an iPhone Duo badge.
Apple hasn't named the day yet. We use 1 April 2027 for now. Check again when Apple names it.

APPLE-18-PLUS-BLOCK.title: Confirm age for apps rated 18+
APPLE-18-PLUS-BLOCK.summary: Apple blocks downloads of apps rated 18+ in these countries. People can download only after their age is confirmed by reasonable means.

GOOGLE-PLAY-BILLING-V8.title: Use Play Billing Library 8 or later
GOOGLE-PLAY-BILLING-V8.summary: New apps and updates need Play Billing Library 8 or later. This starts 31 August 2026. You can ask for more time, up to 1 November 2026. It only affects what you can publish. Apps already live on version 7 can still take payments. That lasts until the 2027 deadline for all apps.

GOOGLE-PLAY-TARGET-API-35.title: Target Android 15 or higher
GOOGLE-PLAY-TARGET-API-35.summary: New apps and updates must target Android 15 (API level 35) or higher. Existing apps must target Android 14, API 34, or higher.

GOOGLE-PLAY-TARGET-API-36.title: Target Android 16 or higher
GOOGLE-PLAY-TARGET-API-36.summary:
New apps and updates must target these levels from 31 August 2026:
- Most apps: Android 16 (API 36) or higher.
- Watch and car apps: API 35 or higher.
- TV and XR headset apps: API 34 or higher.
You can ask for more time in Play Console, up to 1 November 2026.
Existing apps must target API 35 or higher. Otherwise new users on newer devices can't get them.

ANDROID-DEVELOPER-VERIFICATION.title: Register apps to a verified developer
ANDROID-DEVELOPER-VERIFICATION.summary:
From 30 September 2026, apps installed on certified devices there need a verified developer.
- Register in the Android Developer Console.
- Full distribution costs USD 25.
- Free limited accounts cover up to 20 devices.
- Organizations need a D-U-N-S number.
- This goes worldwide in 2027, exact date not yet published.
- Play apps have a separate rule, due 30 September 2026.

GOOGLE-PLAY-PHOTO-VIDEO-PERM.title: Use the photo picker for media
GOOGLE-PLAY-PHOTO-VIDEO-PERM.summary: Only apps that need wide access may ask to see all photos and videos. All other apps must use Android's photo picker.

GOOGLE-PLAY-CHILD-SAFETY.title: Publish your child safety rules
GOOGLE-PLAY-CHILD-SAFETY.summary:
Your app must have these child safety basics:
- Your rules against child sexual abuse and exploitation.
- Put them on a web page anyone, anywhere can open.
- A way for users to give feedback in your app.
- A plan for responding to child sexual abuse material.
- A named person to contact about child safety.

EU-E-EVIDENCE-REGULATION.title: Answer cross-border police requests for user data
EU-E-EVIDENCE-REGULATION.summary:
Police in another EU country can ask you directly for user data.
- Reply within 10 days.
- In an emergency, reply within 8 hours.

EU-WITHDRAWAL-BUTTON-DIRECTIVE.title: Add an easy way to cancel contracts
EU-WITHDRAWAL-BUTTON-DIRECTIVE.summary:
If people can make contracts with you online, including in your app:
- Add a withdrawal button or a withdrawal function.
- Make it easy to see.
- Make it easy to reach.
- It must let people cancel their contract.

EU-GPSR-SAFETY.title: Show maker details and safety warnings
EU-GPSR-SAFETY.summary:
If you sell consumer products in your app or online, show:
- Who made the product.
- The maker's online contact details and postal address.
- Product safety warnings.

GOOGLE-PLAY-CHARGEBACK-COST-SHIFT.title: You pay when buyers dispute Play charges
GOOGLE-PLAY-CHARGEBACK-COST-SHIFT.summary:
For Play orders placed after 3 August 2026, disputed charges cost you.
- You lose the price, minus Google's service fee.
- You also pay the bank's chargeback fee.
- Google covers only its service fee.
- Watch for Google's refund review alerts.
- Fight unfair disputes within 24 hours (Review Refund API).

GOOGLE-ORG-REGISTRATION-REGULATED-CATEGO.title: Some app types need an organization account
GOOGLE-ORG-REGISTRATION-REGULATED-CATEGO.summary:
These apps must be published from an organization account:
- Banking, loans, stock trading and investment funds.
- Crypto wallets and exchanges.
- Medical apps and human research apps.
- VPN apps approved by Google.
- Government apps.
Your business ID number (D-U-N-S) must match your Dun and Bradstreet profile. Apps that don't comply are removed.

GOOGLE-PLAY-APP-PACKAGE-REGISTRATION.title: Register each app's ID with Google
GOOGLE-PLAY-APP-PACKAGE-REGISTRATION.summary: Register every Google Play app's unique ID (package name) in Play Console. This applies worldwide. It's separate from the rules for Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand. Those cover apps installed from outside Google Play. If you don't register, your app may be removed everywhere.

GOOGLE-US-ALT-BILLING-FEE-REPORTING.title: Pay Google fees on outside payments
GOOGLE-US-ALT-BILLING-FEE-REPORTING.summary:
If you're in Google's US program for other payment options or outside links:
- Report your sales to Google.
- Report successful downloads too.
- Pay the Play service fee that applies.
- Start on 1 October 2026.

GOOGLE-PLAY-CATALOG-ACCESS-DEFAULT.title: Other US stores may list your app
GOOGLE-PLAY-CATALOG-ACCESS-DEFAULT.summary: From 22 July 2026, registered US Android app stores can list your app. They get access to Google Play's apps by default. To stop this, opt out in Play Console. Go to Settings, then Catalog Settings.

GOOGLE-CONTACTS-LOCATION-FGS-API37.title: New rules for contacts, location and geofencing
GOOGLE-CONTACTS-LOCATION-FGS-API37.summary:
If your app targets Android 17 (API level 37) or later:
- Read contacts only if the contact picker can't do the core job.
- You must explain why in a form to Google.
- Use Android's location button and its special flag for button location.
- Don't use a foreground service for place alerts. Use the Geofence API.
From 27 October 2026, Play Console flags contacts and location issues before review.

GOOGLE-TECH-QUALITY-FEB-2027.title: Meet new code size and memory limits
GOOGLE-TECH-QUALITY-FEB-2027.summary:
From February 2027, your app must:
- Optimize, shrink and scramble at least 25 percent of its code.
- Use a tool like R8 for this.
- Not keep images in memory while they're off screen.
- Stay under Google's limits for bad memory use.
Google hasn't named the exact day.
If not, Google can limit your app's visibility and publishing.

GOOGLE-RESTORE-CREDENTIALS-APR-2027.title: Keep users signed in on new phones
GOOGLE-RESTORE-CREDENTIALS-APR-2027.summary:
If your app lets people sign in, even if it's optional:
- From April 2027, restore their sign-in when they switch Android phones.
- Use Google's tool for this (Restore Credentials API).
- Google hasn't named the exact day.
- Games don't need to do this for now.

GOOGLE-ANON-CHAT-CHILD-SAFETY-2026.title: Stricter child safety for anonymous chat apps
GOOGLE-ANON-CHAT-CHILD-SAFETY-2026.summary:
